name: Device accounts list
plain: Lets the app list the Google and other accounts signed in on the device.
meaning: Reveals the email addresses of accounts on the phone. Largely replaced by account pickers because the list is an easy way to build an identity profile.

android.store_policy: Play: Google sign-in should use account pickers instead
android.note: Since Android 8.0 (API 26) apps only see accounts they own unless the account owner grants visibility; GET_ACCOUNTS alone no longer shows others.

ios.note: iOS exposes no account list; Sign in with Apple and Credential Provider flows return only the chosen identity.

limits.headline: Can list only its own accounts on Android; iPhone shows no account list
limits.user_action: You tap Choose account or Sign in with Google
can: List the accounts the app itself owns (Android)
Learn about other accounts only when the account owner allows it (Android)
Receive the one identity you pick through Sign in with Apple or an account picker
cannot: See the emails of other accounts on Android 8 and later with the permission alone
See any account list on iPhone
Build a full picture of who you are from the accounts on the phone
limits.reach_label: Own accounts, or the one you pick
limits.differs: Android lists accounts with a prompt but limits what it shows since Android 8; iPhone offers no account list at all.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app see which Google and other accounts are signed in on the phone.
story.for_you: The app can read the email addresses of accounts on your phone. Today most apps instead show an account picker. You may see a sign in pop up with your accounts listed.
story.for_makers: The list helps an app offer a quick login and spot fake accounts. It also hands over the emails of every account on a phone. Platforms have shrunk this so apps now see only accounts they own.

use_cases.example: A social app offers one tap sign in with the Google account on the phone.
A fraud team compares accounts on a phone to spot one phone with hundreds of fake accounts.
A mail app finds your accounts to set up inboxes.
A shopping app pre fills your email at checkout.
An older ad SDK used the account list to link a user across apps.
A game uses the Google Play Games account to save progress.
A work app finds your company account.

story.android_note: Since Android 8 an app only sees accounts it owns unless the account owner grants it more.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no account list. Sign in with Apple and credential flows return only the identity you choose.

technical_bounds: Only user chosen sign in surfaces an account

history.change: getAccounts limited to accounts visible to the app; account visibility APIs added
getAccounts only returns accounts the app can already see
GET_ACCOUNTS became a dangerous Contacts permission
